scope: SFDC_UI, SFDC_Agent and SFDC_BACK; common conversion rules only

sourcePolicies.remoteScreenNova: REST_FIRST; independently authorized same-file archive only after allowed failures
sourcePolicies.remoteScreenKiro: MCP_ONLY; no silent REST, archive or NOVA fallback
sourcePolicies.explicitLocal: LOCAL_FILE; immutable archive hash, page and node
sourcePolicies.story: existing source acquisition preserved; requested Kiro provider/classification/analysis failures are explicit failures

actualNovaValidation.path: REST credential validation -> FIGMA_TOKEN_REQUIRED -> authorized archive -> saved analysis -> generation
actualNovaValidation.note: This proves the missing-credential fallback path, not a successful live REST response. REST-success and rate-limit ordering have separate automated coverage.

pins.componentCompatibility: Pinned NOVA public API/module/token tuple remains mandatory; existing APPLY pre-submit source comparison rejects incompatible same-name Dev Org bundles. No Org deployment was performed.

commonCorrections: Visible standalone popup INSTANCE eligibility requires exact published component and set keys in the pinned release.
Preview-only popup reopen controls never become deployed source.
Kiro receives the source visual acceptance contract; invalid analysis is not replaced with a source-only plan.
Approved text-button geometry covers exact CTA, Primary and Secondary variants; icon/count/unverified/dynamic controls remain excluded.
Nonvisual variable diagnostics do not invalidate identical baked paints; actual paint, size, edge, state and publication checks remain strict.
Full local authored scenes with variable warnings remain reconstructable; partial MCP metadata never becomes an authored scene.
MCP hidden flags are preserved; nested metadata coordinates remain unverified instead of being incorrectly summed.
Partial source coverage cannot become a complete visual pass from a matching root and PNG alone.
Recognized provider-only truncation envelopes fail collection and cached-source validation; ordinary authored JS/JSX/JSON remains intact.
Completed source checkpoints are atomic and scoped to principal/job/file/node; cancellation cannot publish a partial completed index.
Repair retains the best measured candidate and rejects pixel/native/coverage/blocker regressions.

controlledComparison.input: Same retained accepted actual Kiro LWC, same archive/rendered PNG, same pinned library; common deterministic normalization changed
controlledComparison.remaining: Table boundaries/text placement and section-heading text widths remain. No 0.x or global accuracy improvement claim.

recordedMcpReplay.note: Different source contract and unverified revision; not a comparison to the local test or historical 1.x runs. Private harness prompt-label mismatch is disclosed in its separate receipt.

accuracyAndTiming.latencyConclusion: Model generation and repair dominate. Completed collection/analysis reuse and bounded, regression-aware repair are implemented. Native full-scene MCP export and image-input generation require separate verified capabilities, not speculative production changes.

verification.note: Groups overlap and were executed at different implementation stages; they must not be added into a single test total. The final relevant Workbench and source/quality groups passed after the final mapping changes.

backendFullSuite.classification: All 21 failing cases reproduced with identical failure fingerprints on the unchanged baseline; separate receipt retained.

externalLimits: Figma MCP View-seat tool quota blocked further fresh source collection and the audited read-only JSON_REST_V1 feasibility probe.
Full authored properties/publication keys/planning descriptions and original revision are not proven by metadata plus reference code.
Current headless analysis/generation is text-only; collection images and external PNG validation do not mean vision-assisted generation.
Live provider expiry/revocation was not forced on the retained user grant; independent-process reuse was verified and revoke/isolation have automated coverage.

No new SFDC_UI interactive sign-in or real Org deployment was claimed; the existing Salesforce screen was observed, service health/auth binding verified, and Salesforce credentials/configuration were not changed.
